title: „Way-to-Work“: Digital aftercare after vocational rehabilitation
summary:
Mental disorders are the most common cause of occupational disability and retirement. There are high costs for treatments with consequences for the quality of life and self-esteem of those affected. At the end of professional rehabilitation, people with mental illness face major challenges. There is a lack of structurally established aftercare that can contribute to long-term stabilization. Digital aftercare offers promising flexible and needs-oriented support during the transition to everyday (working) life after the end of rehabilitation. To date, no research has been conducted into digital aftercare for people with mental disorders with a focus on professional reintegration. As part of the study “Way-to-Work”, a digital aftercare program should be developed and evaluated with regard to the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of the intervention. For this purpose, 160 participants will be recruited and randomly assigned to the intervention or control group. The intervention group will receive 12 months of access to the digital intervention. It is expected that participation in the intervention group will be associated with a higher general level of functioning, less psychological distress, better quality of life and increased work-related motivation. Furthermore, a higher proportion of working people in the general labor market is expected in the intervention group. 
If “Way-to-Work” proves to be effective, the digital aftercare could be structurally established with relatively little effort.

interventions.name:
The intervention group takes part in the internet-based aftercare program “Way-to-Work” for twelve months.
Data collection takes place at the end of professional rehabilitation and six, twelve and eighteen months after the end of the measure.

The control group does not receive access to the digital aftercare program. Other existing treatment options are available without restriction. Data collection also takes place at the end of vocational rehabilitation and six, twelve and eighteen months after the end of the measure.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- DRV Baden-Württemberg
- F-diagnosis
- Duration of treatment of at least 6 months (or shorter if there is an employment relationship)
Exclusion criteria:
- acute suicidality
- no internet access
- insufficient knowledge of German
